headline: Ripple's CEO says Saylor's Bitcoin strategy has hurt crypto, as Fear & Greed hits 15
summary: The day's sharpest story wasn't price action — it was Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse publicly criticizing Michael Saylor's Bitcoin-maximalist approach, arguing it has damaged the broader crypto market. Bitcoin itself barely moved, holding near $60,316, while Solana was the standout gainer in the top 15, up 3.15%. The Fear & Greed index sits at 15 — deep in Extreme Fear territory — reflecting a market that has been under sustained selling pressure for weeks.

winners.name: LAB
winners.catalyst: No specific catalyst identified for LAB's 5.73% gain — the move appears to be technical, with no named event or announcement driving it.

losers.name: Worldcoin
losers.catalyst: Worldcoin fell 2.85% as investor interest rotated toward AI stocks, pulling capital away from AI-adjacent crypto projects.

whyItMoved:
Price action was quiet across the board today — Bitcoin gained 0.30%, Ethereum 0.95%, and most top-15 assets moved less than 1% in either direction. The real story was off-chain. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse publicly criticized Michael Saylor's Bitcoin-maximalist strategy, arguing that Saylor's approach — which involves MicroStrategy accumulating Bitcoin at scale and advocating that institutions hold only BTC — has actively hurt the broader crypto market by crowding out altcoins and narrowing institutional attention. Garlinghouse said he remains bullish on Bitcoin itself, but the criticism landed as a notable public split between two prominent figures in the industry.

Solana was the standout mover in the top 15, up 3.15% on the day. According to a report from The Block, SOL climbed roughly 9% over the past week — that figure comes from the news report rather than verified 24-hour price data, but it aligns with the broader momentum visible in Solana-linked equities, which gained double digits over the same period.

Worldcoin's 2.85% decline fits a pattern noted this week: investor interest has been rotating toward AI stocks, pulling capital away from AI-adjacent crypto projects like WLD. Dogecoin and Hyperliquid were also cited as weekly underperformers for the same reason.

The Fear & Greed index reading of 15 reflects sustained selling pressure accumulated over recent weeks — a level consistent with prolonged drawdown periods rather than a single-session shock.
worthKnowing: Spain's financial regulator told Binance and other crypto firms there will be no exceptions or deadline extensions for MiCA compliance — the EU's crypto regulatory framework — with the deadline now imminent.

A U.S. House Democrat who may soon chair a key financial committee publicly condemned the inclusion of crypto in 401(k) retirement plans, a stance that could shape the legislative environment for crypto in workplace savings accounts.
Dogecoin and Hyperliquid's HYPE were among the week's worst performers in the top tier, with analysts pointing to capital rotating into AI equities as the proximate cause.
